title: request-scoping-janitor-and-telemetry-shim-for-polyglot-sdks
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: different language SDKs currently leak stale request contexts when async work outlives the originating HTTP request (serverless cold paths + background workers). This causes inflated tail latency, mis-attributed spans, and noisy error signals in the Console.

Goal: implement a small runtime-safe 'scoping janitor' plus a telemetry shim that works across Node/Python/Go SDKs to ensure request-scoped metadata (trace ID, sampling hints, route tags) is (a) deterministically closed when the logical request ends, (b) recorded to a short-lived 'orphan' bucket if async work continues so telemetry doesn't overwrite newer requests, and (c) cheap to run in hot fast-paths.

Why now: recent postmortem on INC-2026-02 showed multiple production incidents where background KV-cache refresh tasks produced spans attributed to unrelated requests. This ticket is a low-risk infra change that will materially reduce false positives in the latency/error dashboards and improve SLO math for low-latency customers.
acceptance_criteria: Polyglot SDKs (Node, Python, Go) include a scoping janitor that marks request boundaries and emits a deterministic CLOSE event
Requests that finish before async continuation do not leave active trace context attached to pool-worker spans (verified by integration test harness)
Console shows separate 'orphan' telemetry bucket for traces emitted after CLOSE with a configurable retention/flag
No measurable CPU or p99 latency regression in SDK microbenchmarks (<1% overhead in hot-path benchmarks)
E2E regression test added to CI; rollout gated behind feature flag per runtime and gradual ramp to 100% using runtime-1.18 release channel
implementation_notes:
Approach: add a tiny opaque RequestScope object created at HTTP ingress. RequestScope exposes .close() and registers a weak-ref finalizer in languages that have them. When .close() is called we stamp the scope state to CLOSED and set an ephemeral flag on the tracing carrier. If async work tries to start a new span after CLOSE, the shim routes the span to an 'orphan' envelope with metadata: origin_request_id, closed_at, runtime_hint.

SDK changes: Node: use AsyncLocalStorage + FinalizationRegistry; Python: contextvars + weakref.finalize; Go: explicit context.WithValue + deferred janitor that sets closed marker on context. The shim should be installed as the first middleware in HTTP adapters and included as default in our hosted frameworks quickstarts.

Rollout: behind config map feature flag "scoping_janitor_enabled". Start with canary on dedicated-internal org, then 10% hosted, 50%, 100%. Add per-org opt-out for legacy integrations.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives:
Alternatives considered: (1) strict instrumentation policy to forbid background spans using server request ID — rejected because breaking for many customers who rely on background tasks; (2) central proxy-level enforcement that cuts spans at network boundary — rejected due to incompatibility with in-process background work and risk of dropping valid telemetry.

Tradeoffs: this approach is SDK-heavy and requires updates across runtimes. That increases lift but allows precise attribution and keeps network overhead minimal. There is a small risk of edge cases where finalizers fire late and mark still-relevant work as orphaned; mitigated by shining visibility into the orphan bucket and short retention for orphan metrics by default.
testing_plan: Unit tests per SDK verifying CLOSED marker behavior; integration harness that simulates HTTP request lifecycle with continuations and worker pool; load test comparing p50/p95/p99 token generation latency and CPU cost with/without janitor. Create synthetic traces in staging Console to validate orphan bucket separation and dashboard filters. Add metric: telemetry.scoping_janitor.orphan_rate and a dashboard tile to monitor during rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge SDK changes behind feature flag. 2) Deploy Node/Python/Go  canary packages to internal org. 3) Enable feature flag for dedicated-internal and run 48h smoke tests checking orphan_rate, sampling alignment, and CPU. 4) Gradual ramp to hosted customers: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days with automatic rollback on error budget burn or orphan_rate spike > 5x baseline. 5) Post-rollout: mark feature GA and remove flag after 90 days.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add alerts: alarm if telemetry.scoping_janitor.orphan_rate increases > 5x baseline for >15m; alert on sample_mismatch_count > 100/min. Add Console dashboard tile showing orphan traces by origin, runtime, and route. Add trace-quality regression alert if routing causes >1% drop in trace-sampling similarity for top 20 routes.
risks: Edge-case finalizer timing causing misclassification of long-lived valid work
Customer code that intentionally reuses request context across requests could see changed attribution
SDK adoption lag — rollout complexity across language ecosystems
